title: Rust TUI rewrite
description:
Replace bash+zellij+tmux stack with custom ratatui TUI. Core motivation: activity detection is impossible with zellij (no API for pane output events). Custom PTY handling gives us full control over the UX.

Key libraries: ratatui, portable-pty, vt100

See docs/architecture-research.md for full analysis.

title: Scaffold Rust project with dependencies
description:
# Scaffold Rust project with dependencies

Initialize the Rust project with all dependencies needed for the TUI rewrite.

## Context

This is the first ticket in the Rust TUI rewrite. We are replacing the bash+zellij+tmux stack with a custom ratatui-based TUI. This ticket sets up the project structure and dependencies.

## Implementation

### Files to Create

- `Cargo.toml` — Project manifest with dependencies
- `src/main.rs` — Entry point stub
- `src/lib.rs` — Library root (optional, for clean separation)

### Dependencies

```toml
[package]
name = "bz"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
ratatui = "0.29"
crossterm = "0.28"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }
tui-term = "0.3"
portable-pty = "0.9"
vt100 = "0.15"
color-eyre = "0.6"
```

### Patterns

Use `color-eyre` for error handling:
```rust
use color_eyre::eyre::Result;

fn main() -> Result<()> {
    color_eyre::install()?;
    // ...
    Ok(())
}
```

### Project Structure

```
src/
├── main.rs      # Entry point, calls run()
└── lib.rs       # App struct, run function (optional)
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cargo build` succeeds
- [ ] `cargo run` executes without panic (can be empty/stub)
- [ ] All dependencies resolve correctly

## Gotchas

- tui-term 0.3 requires ratatui 0.29+ (check compatibility)
- portable-pty 0.9 was released Feb 2025, should be latest

Test with target applications
description:
# Test with target applications

Verify terminal emulation works correctly with all target apps.

## Context

The definition specifies these apps must render correctly:
- Claude Code
- iamb (Matrix client)
- OpenCode  
- vim/neovim
- tmux
- Standard shells (bash, zsh, fish)

This ticket is for systematic testing and fixing any issues.

## Implementation

### Test Matrix

| App | Feature | Expected | Notes |
|-----|---------|----------|-------|
| bash | Basic commands | ✓ | ls, cd, cat |
| bash | Colors | ✓ | ls --color, prompt colors |
| bash | Readline | ✓ | Arrow keys, history, Ctrl+R |
| vim | Startup | ✓ | Opens without errors |
| vim | Editing | ✓ | Insert mode, navigation |
| vim | Colors | ✓ | Syntax highlighting |
| vim | Mouse | ✓ | Click to position cursor |
| vim | Resize | ✓ | Redraws on window resize |
| tmux | Startup | ✓ | Creates session |
| tmux | Splits | ✓ | Panes render correctly |
| tmux | Prefix key | ✓ | Ctrl+B works (via Ctrl+B b) |
| Claude Code | Startup | ✓ | TUI initializes |
| Claude Code | Streaming | ✓ | Output streams smoothly |
| Claude Code | Syntax | ✓ | Code blocks render |
| Claude Code | Bell | ✓ | Notifications detected |
| iamb | Startup | ✓ | TUI initializes |
| iamb | Messages | ✓ | Chat renders correctly |

### Testing Process

1. Launch bz with test config
2. For each app, run through the test cases
3. Document any failures with screenshots/logs
4. Fix issues or create follow-up tickets

### Common Issues to Watch For

- **Cursor positioning** — Apps that use absolute cursor positioning
- **Alternate screen** — Apps that switch to/from alternate buffer
- **Colors** — 256 color and true color support
- **Unicode** — Wide characters, emoji
- **Mouse** — Apps that expect mouse input

### Debugging Tips

```rust
// Add debug logging for escape sequences
env_logger::init();
log::debug\!("PTY output: {:?}", &data[..n.min(100)]);
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All apps in test matrix work or have documented issues
- [ ] Critical apps (vim, tmux, Claude Code) fully functional
- [ ] Any discovered issues have tickets for follow-up

## Gotchas

- Some issues may be in vt100 crate, not our code
- TERM environment variable matters (set to xterm-256color)
- Some apps detect terminal capabilities via terminfo

title: UX: rethink channel state indicators

Current approach may have inverted semantics vs Slack mental model (white = unread there).

Ideas to explore:
- Grey/white = "have you visited since last stdout"
- Spinner animation = work in progress
- Red dot = actual notification needing action
- Or other visual language that's more intuitive

Need to think through what states actually matter and how to communicate them clearly.
